Research Seminar
Particle-resolved multiscale simulation of sulfide all-solid-state composite 
cathodes:
from powder packing to transport

2Battery Materials Lab.
 Heterogeneous-technology pipeline for a sulfide composite 
cathode
• Three particle-level stages, each calibrated to its own experiment — never to one 
another.
• Agreement between stages is treated as cross-validation; disagreement as a quantified 
model limit.
Introduction
< DEM → MPM → voxel transport → electrode response >

3Battery Materials Lab.
 Soft-sphere DEM reproduces the composition dependence of 
porosity
• Rigid spheres with a linear hysteretic contact law, pressed to 300 MPa; one bed per 
composition.
• Porosity 31.8 → 25.1 → 16.7 → 16.5 % through one run; 7:3 (large : small NCM) is the 
densest of five.
DEM
< four stages of one 7:3 bed (0 · 47 · 296 · 165 MPa) > < porosity vs large : small NCM >

4Battery Materials Lab.
 From the contact network to Li⁺ transport: a Kirchhoff network 
with contact constriction
• Each SE–SE contact = bulk resistance + Hertz constriction; σ₀ = 1.5 mS cm⁻¹ (pellet 
literature range).
• Transport tortuosity 7.2 → 5.0 (0:10 → 7:3): 73–75 % of the resistance sits in the contact 
necks, not in path length.

5Battery Materials Lab.
 What a rigid-sphere DEM cannot do
• No shape change and no yield cap: overlap is the only proxy for plasticity, so the 18× 
softened SE modulus (24 → 1.35 GPa) is a surrogate, not a property.
• During compression, global viscous damping carries 58 % of the plate reaction in one 
7:3 bed — an open issue.
DEM
Battery-electrode DEM literature 
(22 studies)
· softened SE modulus: 0 of 22
· yield / hardness cap: 7 of 22
· linear hysteretic law: 1 of 22
· global damping during dry 
compaction: none reported
< hysteretic normal force (code reproduction) >

6Battery Materials Lab.
 The material point method supplies the plastic half
• J2 plasticity on a background grid: true shape change and void filling that a rigid sphere 
cannot represent.
• Active material is kept rigid (DEM skeleton); only the electrolyte flows.

7Battery Materials Lab.
MPM
 How the electrolyte parameters were fixed
• Bulk modulus from DFT; shear softening calibrated to pure-electrolyte compaction; 
yield stress from the LPSCl literature range.
Three layers of the SE model
• Real bulk: E ≈ 24 GPa, σy 0.05–0.30 GPa 
(single-crystal LPSCl range)
• DEM effective: E = 1.35 GPa (18× 
softened) — reproduces compaction, not a 
property
• MPM: E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 0.30 
GPa; K = 25.5 GPa ≈ DFT bulk modulus 
26.2 GPa
What is — and is not — an external 
anchor
• Pure-SE porosity 10 % at 300 MPa is the 
calibration target: a lab reference sample, 
unpublished
• It is not a literature anchor; the earlier 
citation was retracted
• Shear-only softening keeps the real bulk 
modulus (ν = 0.49); softening the bulk over-
crushed the bed
The softening is irreducible for a resolved-grain continuum — a volumetric cap and real E 
both failed the Heckel test.

8Battery Materials Lab.
 DEM-scaffold MPM: what agrees, and what does not count as 
evidence
• Stress-stop thickness agrees (30.7 vs 30.3 µm); porosity agreement is not independent 
— the AM skeleton and the SE seeds both come from the DEM bed.
• Pressed honestly to 300 MPa the MPM over-compacts (sphere porosity 1.1 % vs 15.6 % 
measured): AM load sharing is the missing piece.

9Battery Materials Lab.
 Voxelizing the compacted microstructure turns morphology into a 
transport mesh
• Finite-volume ∇·(σ∇φ) = 0 on the phase grid gives ionic, electronic and thermal 
conductivity on the same structure.
• Faces are joined by a harmonic mean, so there is no interface-resistance term: the voxel 
solver sits on the contact-free branch.

10Battery Materials Lab.
 Additives enter at the voxel stage
• Carbon fibres (VGCF) as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-line insulator, 
a conductive polymer as true-diameter spheres.
• A 104-arm pre-registered run: the electronic-conductivity order across 1–4 wt% VGCF is 
robust to voxel size and origin shift (72/72).
Transport
< fibre + binder seeds > < additive stamps > < σ(e⁻) vs VGCF wt%, three voxel sizes >

11Battery Materials Lab.
 Problem 1 — the voxel electronic gain is grid-dependent and does 
not extrapolate
• Same bed pair, same convention, voxel 0.4 → 0.3 → 0.25 µm: the electronic ratio keeps 
falling and the ionic ratio changes sign.
• The increments follow no power law — no Richardson extrapolation, and no lower-bound 
claim either.
Limits
What survives
· the headline of the earlier manuscript draft is a 
grid artefact
· the shape (monotonic, decelerating) is real; no 
converged value yet
· finer grids reach the memory limit of one GPU
< conductivity ratio vs voxel size >

12Battery Materials Lab.
 Problem 2 — absolute electronic conductivity sits far above DC-
polarization measurements
• Voxel model 54 and 71 vs 4.5 and 12 mS cm⁻¹ measured (×12, ×5.7): no interface 
resistance, unanchored carbon conductivity.
• Carbon- and binder-free NCM–SE beds, common NCM reference 4.1 mS cm⁻¹: 0.38–0.47 
mS cm⁻¹ across the five compositions.
Limits
< voxel model vs experiment (log scale) > < NCM–SE beds, common-conductivity network >

13Battery Materials Lab.
 Problem 3 — compaction mechanics: over-compaction and load 
sharing
• Large–large NCM contacts carry 48–60 % of the vertical stress; 7:3 is the minimum.
• Its five-composition order matches the measured porosity order (n = 5, exploratory; the 
experimental set is a selected subset).
Limits
< contribution to σzz by contact type > < SE von Mises stress, four stages (0–150 MPa) >

14Battery Materials Lab.
Progress
 Pre-registered, origin-replicated runs — what each one settled
• Every production run is registered before launch (hypotheses, decision lines, 
sealed code) and judged by an independent reviewer.
Registered 
campaigns
1. 8-arm origin factorial, voxel 0.15 µm gain follows the represented additive 
volume (procedure and verdict only)
2. Phase A: 104 arms, VGCF 1–4 wt% order robust, 72/72; replay 0.00000 %
3. Lee-2025 absolute comparison, 16 arms R = 2.07 → order-of-magnitude 
agreement; Q = 0.84 → prediction met
4. 194 LHS beds → descriptor dataset v1.2 sealed pipeline; 7 external re-
verification rounds before launch
Ratios and gains of the 8-arm series are on hold — only the procedure and the verdict are 
reported.

15Battery Materials Lab.
 A 194-bed design-of-experiments dataset for machine learning
• 130 + 64 Latin-hypercube beds (composition, particle sizes, loading) → structure and 
transport descriptors, released as v1.2.
• SE percolation 106/130; geometric tortuosity 1.3–4.2 (shortest path, not transport); 
porosity OOF R² 0.99 (collaborator) vs 0.98 from the five design knobs.
Progress
< geometric tortuosity > < ionically isolated AM > < porosity vs SE fraction >

16Battery Materials Lab.
Plan
 Next steps — closing the three problems
• Each item is registered before it is run; nothing below has a result yet.
Transport
• Interface resistance in the voxel solver: 
AM–AM film implemented (default off), 
production on hold
• Anchor the carbon conductivity with the 
SBE/DBE DC-polarization values (re-run 
registered)
• Polycrystalline vs single-crystal NCM 
conductivity: literature first, then the model
Mechanics and mixing
• AM load sharing in the MPM platen 
(registered contract)
• Stepwise unloading of the five beds: 
springback vs measured thickness 
(registration revised twice)
• Coating-aware mixing: surface-energy 
anchor for SE–SE adhesion before the 
confirmatory runs
Decisions pending: launch of the 194 + 20 network batch after the final external check.

17Battery Materials Lab.
Summary
 What the pipeline can and cannot say today
• DEM + contact network: composition trends in porosity, Li⁺ transport and 
load sharing — one bed per composition, model-internal ratios.
• MPM: plastic morphology and the stress-stop thickness; porosity agreement 
is not independent evidence.
• Voxel transport: a contact-free upper branch; electronic gains are grid-
dependent and absolute values exceed measurements.
• Every production number is pre-registered, sealed and externally re-verified 
before it is reported.
